title: The game heap is a fixed 11 MiB from the build: with 128 MB of RAM Vivec still runs under the 2 MiB safety gap and loads pause
status: Fixed in v0.0.45 (branch v0.0.43-prefetch, merged in the v0.0.45 line): the heap is sized at start from the largest free Fast RAM block less CHIM margin (2 MiB + an eighth), grown by a quarter of the room beyond the built 11 MiB when that room holds it plus 8 MiB, at most 24 MiB; -heapmb as asked, aw_autoram 0 keeps the built size. FS-UAE, dev2 data, 128 MiB: a 24 MiB heap and an 82 MiB CHIM cache; no hunk-gap safety warning in 5 laps of Balmora, Caldera, Vivec and Seyda Neen (dev2 as built: 4 warnings on one open-world route); 16 MiB keeps 11 MiB.
where: engine heap size (sys_amiga.c Sys_Init); Vivec city warns 'hunk-gap safety below 2 MiB'
severity_reason: players with more RAM get no benefit: memory warnings and load pauses that spare RAM could avoid

title: CHIM terrain records were stored whole: 489.4 MB of the v0.0.46 world's frame segments
status: Fixed in v0.0.47: world format 0.11 (generated terrain records, --chim-terrain-pack generate) is written by default since v0.0.47 (decided for the project, 21 October 2026). Measured on the v0.0.46 world: of its 1,315 MB of frame segments, 489.4 MB were terrain records; format 0.10 (compact records) would take them to 450.8 MB, format 0.11 to 247.6 MB, with 95,818 of 97,369 terrain records generated and every tenth of each kind checked byte for byte through the engine's generator. Recorded as an entry from the bug journal on 16 November 2026.
where: CHIM world format: the terrain records of the frame segments
severity_reason: world size and read volume; nothing wrong is drawn

history.note: World format 0.11: the converter's own triangles generated too: The 0.11 generator (still experimental and off) now also makes the records of the converter's own triangles (shoreline and 32-unit detail tiles) from the chunk's 32-unit samples and the triangles, stored as record version 2. On the v0.0.46 world 95,818 of 97,369 terrain records are generated (was 83,236), every tenth of each kind checked through the engine's generator byte for byte, and the terrain records would go from 489.4 MB to 247.6 MB. Not generated yet: 563 lava records, 886 too large for the engine's loading buffer, and 100 whose texture mappings differ.

World format 0.11: texture splits and water crossings generated too: The 0.11 generator (still experimental and off) now also makes the ground polygons the builder cuts where their texture span passes 240 texels and where the water line crosses a tile: on the v0.0.46 world 83,236 of 97,369 terrain records are generated (was 77,020), every tenth checked through the engine's generator byte for byte, and the terrain records would go from 489.4 MB to 298.5 MB. Not generated yet: the 13,284 records holding the converter's own triangles, 738 lava-bed and shore records, and 183 others.

World format 0.11: generated terrain records, off by default: World format 0.11 is in the source behind `--chim-terrain-pack generate` (experimental, off; needs terrain references): a regular-path terrain record stored as its corner heights and a few decided facts, from which the engine generates the render part of the chunk, the same bytes as the stored record. The planes and the standing hull stay stored (the hull is qbsp's compiled union). Host tests only; on the v0.0.46 world 77,020 of 97,369 terrain records are generated, every tenth of them checked through the engine's generator byte for byte, and the terrain records would go from 489.4 MB to 310.4 MB. The shoreline, lava and converter-triangle records are not generated yet.
